plans.note: Section 15 is expressly headed 'Limitation of Garman's Liability' — check for one-sided (vendor-only) cap, cap amount versus fees paid, exclusion of consequential damages, and whether IP indemnity (sec-13), confidentiality (sec-14) and wilful misconduct are carved out. Warranty disclaimers in sec-12 may interact.

Section 13 is the IP indemnity from Garman; assess scope (defence plus costs), procedure, and whether it is capped by sec-15. Look for any reciprocal or customer-side indemnity hidden in sec-3 restrictions or sec-20 general matters; note absence of a misconduct/personal-injury indemnity if none appears.

A software licence of this type rarely restricts the customer's business lines; check sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) and sec-20 (General Matters) for any covenant limiting products we may buy or build before concluding it is absent.

Check the licence grant (sec-2), use restrictions (sec-3) and maintenance (sec-10) for any sole-source or exclusive-supply undertaking requiring us to take routing software or support only from Garman; likely none.

Fees (sec-11) and maintenance pricing (sec-10) are the only plausible homes for an MFN. Only flag if we are obliged to give Garman our best terms; an MFN running in our favour is welcome and must not be flagged.

Section 19 is squarely on point. Test mutuality, duration (12 months preferred, 24 tolerable), whether it is limited to personnel actually engaged under the agreement, and whether general advertising/unsolicited applicants are carved out.

Section 17 (Term and Termination) is primary; also review the rejection option in sec-7/sec-8 and any maintenance cancellation right in sec-10. Check whether we may terminate on notice without penalty and whether Garman has a symmetrical convenience right we should resist.
Maintenance terms typically auto-renew: check sec-10 and sec-17 for renewal mechanics, the non-renewal notice window (60 days or less preferred) and any uncapped uplift in the sec-11 fee provisions.

Governing law, venue and any arbitration or dispute clause will sit in General Matters (sec-20). Confirm the chosen law is New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration; note a merely accepted (not preferred) law in the rationale only.

Assignment is normally in sec-20; check we may assign to affiliates and to a successor in a merger/change of control without consent, and that Garman has no termination right triggered by our change of control (cross-check sec-17).

Ownership language will sit in the licence grant (sec-2) and escrow (sec-16). Confirm our data (including converted data under sec-4) and any customisations we pay for are ours, that Confidential Information in sec-14 covers our data, and that no clause assigns our IP or feedback to Garman.

Section 2 grants the licence and sec-3 restricts use. Check that affiliates, authorised locations and outsourced contractors are covered, that the licence is perpetual/irrevocable once fees are paid, and that restrictions do not bar third-party operation or disaster recovery copies.

Any licence-verification or inspection right against us would sit with the use restrictions (sec-3) or general matters (sec-20); if present, test frequency, notice, business-hours limits and who bears cost. May well be absent in this drafting.

Look for interest on late payment, early-termination charges or stipulated damages payable by us in sec-11 and sec-17. Credits or remedies running to us (e.g. refunds on rejection under sec-8) are favourable and must not be flagged.

Section 12 (Specifications and Warranty) is primary; read with acceptance testing (sec-6), rejection rights (sec-7/sec-8) and maintenance (sec-10). Check warranty duration, conformance-to-specification standard, the remedy (repair/replace then refund) and any broad disclaimer.

No insurance heading appears in the outline; check sec-20 general matters and the on-site implementation provisions (sec-4, sec-9) before recording as missing, since Garman personnel attend our locations.

Check sec-11 fees and sec-10 maintenance for any committed seat/location count, minimum annual spend or take-or-pay support term; licence-fee instalments for a perpetual licence are not a minimum commitment.

Post-termination consequences should be in sec-17 with survival in sec-18; escrow (sec-16) and the confidentiality return-of-materials duty (sec-14) are partial substitutes. Confirm we get our data back in a usable format and reasonable exit assistance, and flag as missing if only Garman's materials must be returned.
